reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports the first three premises by showing that μO, controlled via T and PO2, governs the stability of reference oxides and enables pure rocksalt HEO synthesis. However, it does not address nanoparticles, selective oxidation of metallic constituents, or the direct link to catalytic/thermoelectric performance, leaving the last two premises unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Oxygen chemical potential (μO) can be tuned by temperature and oxygen partial pressure (PO2)
Lower μO stabilizes lower-oxidation-state oxides (e.g., MnO, FeO) over higher ones (Mn2O3, Fe2O3)
This stabilization enables synthesis of single-phase high-entropy oxides (HEOs) under low PO2
The same μO control can be applied to multi-element nanoparticles to prevent selective oxidation of reactive metals
Preventing selective oxidation preserves the homogeneous solid-solution structure and functional properties
